title: Hybrid films loaded with 5-fluorouracil and Reglan for synergistic treatment of colon cancer via asynchronous dual-drug

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 2 (Materials/Drug description): "Reglan is also called metoclopramide or Chloramphenicol"
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Reglan is the trade name of metoclopramide (C14H22ClN3O2), an antiemetic. Chloramphenicol is a completely different compound (an antibiotic, C11H12Cl2N2O5). The text identifies the same substance as two chemically unrelated drugs, which is factually wrong and internally contradictory (the stated formula and the antiemetic pharmacology correspond only to metoclopramide).

The chemical name given does not correspond to the stated molecular formula C14H22ClN3O2. Metoclopramide is 4-amino-5-chloro-N-[2-(diethylamino)ethyl]-2-methoxybenzamide; the ethyl linker is omitted, so the name as written describes a different (and non-existent as drawn) molecule.

predicted_errors.error_location: Title, Abstract, Keywords ("synergistic treatment of colon cancer", "tumor-targeted therapy")
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The only evidence presented is morphology (SEM/TEM), XRD/FTIR and in vitro dissolution. No cell-line, cytotoxicity, synergy (e.g., combination index) or animal/tumor-targeting data are reported, and Reglan is an antiemetic with no anticancer action, so it cannot act 'synergistically' against colon cancer. Likewise, nothing in the formulation (PVP matrix + non-pH-responsive CA) confers colon or tumor targeting; the dissolution protocol only mimics gastric (pH 2) and intestinal (pH 7) fluids.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 2 (in vitro dissolution): "No mutual interference was observed between the dissolutions of Reglan and 5-FU due to the blank CA coating in the core–shell particles."
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Both drugs are quantified by UV–vis absorbance of the same bulk medium. A blank CA shell cannot prevent spectral overlap of two drugs that are simultaneously present in the dissolution medium; the stated justification is a non sequitur, and no wavelength/selectivity validation (e.g., non-overlapping λmax, calibration in mixed medium) is provided.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 2 (in vitro dissolution): "an equivalent volume of sodium hydroxide was subsequently added to the dissolution media to adjust the pH to 7.0"
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: If an 'equivalent volume' (i.e., 600 mL) of NaOH solution is added to the 600 mL of 0.01 N HCl, the medium volume doubles, which dilutes the sampled drug concentrations by a factor of two. The paper states only that 5.0 mL samples are replaced with 'equal volumes of fresh media ... to maintain constant volumes' and never accounts for the volume/dilution change at the pH switch, so the reported cumulative release calculations cannot be reproduced as described.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 2 (in vitro dissolution): "in accordance with the Chinese Pharmacopoeia (2020 Ed.) ... seven vessels ... 37°C ± 1°C"
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The protocol claims conformity with the Chinese Pharmacopoeia paddle method, but pharmacopoeial paddle testing uses six units and a medium temperature of 37 ± 0.5 °C. The stated 'seven vessels' and ±1 °C tolerance contradict the cited standard (and seven vessels is also inconsistent with the three samples S2, S3, S4 described).

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 2 (Working fluids) vs. Figure 3A (blank CA particles S1)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The Methods state that 'four working fluids were determined' and then list only the monolithic 5-FU/CA fluid, the core fluid, the shell fluid and the casting suspension. No preparation conditions (composition, flow rate, voltage) are given for sample S1, the blank CA particles whose SEM image and size distribution are nevertheless reported in Figure 3A and 3G, so that sample cannot be reproduced.

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction, last paragraph: "Reglan is designed to be released in a pulsatile manner" vs. Abstract: "fast release of Reglan"
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: A 'pulsatile' release implies a programmed lag followed by a burst, whereas the mechanism actually described (immediate dissolution of the water/acid-soluble PVP K30 matrix, erosion mechanism) is simple immediate/fast release. The two descriptions of the same release stage are inconsistent.

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction: "This finding is attributed to the fact that the core-shell medicated particles are often reported to be widely prepared using bottom-up chemical synthesis methods, which make it difficult for creating core-sheath nanofibers."
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The stated explanation is logically broken: the prevalence of bottom-up chemical synthesis of core-shell particles has no bearing on the difficulty of making core-sheath nanofibers, and it does not explain the reported disparity in publication counts (1,421 vs 59).

predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract: "X-ray diffraction and Fourier-transform infrared tests verified that the Reglan and 5-FU ... showed amorphous states and fine compatibilities"
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: FTIR cannot establish an amorphous physical state (only molecular interactions/compatibility), and XRD alone cannot establish 'fine compatibility'. Attributing both conclusions jointly to both techniques overstates what each measurement can demonstrate.
